decisiveFinding.headline: The dispatch's named fix mechanism is factually impossible, independent of the diagnosis being correct. stampCountyZoning() (legacy-design-tools) writes ONLY to txgio_parcel (zoning-stamp-db.ts:138-145, a raw UPDATE keyed on county_fips+feature_index) and never references tx_zoning_district_staging anywhere in the file or anywhere else in the repo (whole-repo grep: 2 hits, both comments, zero code paths). It also runs against a different database connection (DATABASE_URL, legacy-design-tools' own store) than tx_zoning_district_staging's real store (CORTEX_DATABASE_URL / neondb).
decisiveFinding.realWritePath: tx_zoning_district_staging is populated exclusively by hauska-engine's packages/engine-core/scripts/stage-tx-zoning-district.mjs, which fetches live ArcGIS FeatureServer polygons per hauska-engine's OWN city registry (packages/engine-core/src/zoning-staging/registry.ts) with REPLACE-by-city_key semantics, gated behind ZONING_STAGING_PATH=1 and --apply, against CORTEX_DATABASE_URL. This is a different repo, a different registry, and a different mechanism than anything this dispatch scoped.
decisiveFinding.compoundingGap: hauska-engine's ZONING_STAGING_REGISTRY currently has exactly 2 entries (elgin-tx, layer 0 only; smithville-tx). There is no Travis-side layer-1 entry there at all, and the registry keys one entry per cityKey -- so staging layer 1 requires a NEW hauska-engine registry entry (mirroring CTX-ELGIN's own legacy-design-tools zoning-layers.ts addition) before any staging run could even target it.

leave_behind.text: In this pipeline, a dispatch's phrase 'the existing stamp path' can name a real, working function that nonetheless writes to the wrong table for the stated goal -- stampCountyZoning() genuinely works (CTX-ELGIN proved it, PR #643) but only ever touches txgio_parcel, never tx_zoning_district_staging. A file pointer being real and functional is not evidence it reaches the table a later mission needs; check the actual write target (grep for the destination table's literal name across the whole repo, not just near the named function) before treating a 'staging writer' claim as ground truth.

This pipeline has TWO independent, non-syncing zoning-district signals for the same city: legacy-design-tools' txgio_parcel.zoning_district (stamped in-memory via lib/cad-ingest/src/txgio/zoning-layers.ts) and hauska-engine's tx_zoning_district_staging (ETL'd from live ArcGIS via packages/engine-core/src/zoning-staging/registry.ts). They have separate registries, separate DB connections, and separate repos -- a fix landed in one's registry (as CTX-ELGIN did) has zero effect on the other's coverage. Any future 'wire this GIS layer' mission should state explicitly which of the two registries it means, since both currently exist for Elgin (one complete for layer 1, one not).

As of 2026-09-09 (this session, live read-only query): tx_zoning_district_staging holds 3,220 rows for city_key='elgin-tx' (layer_role='base', county 48021, source_layer_id=0) and ZERO rows for Elgin under county 48453 (Travis) at any city_key or layer_role. Travis county's only staged cities today: austin-tx (21,953), lakeway-tx (749), pflugerville-tx (725).

As of 2026-09-09: hauska-engine's packages/engine-core/src/zoning-staging/registry.ts ZONING_STAGING_REGISTRY has exactly 2 entries total (elgin-tx -> FeatureServer/0 only; smithville-tx), keyed strictly one entry per cityKey (registry.ts:118-132, resolveZoningStagingCity throws if a key is missing). No Travis-side Elgin entry exists.

The actual fix: add a new hauska-engine ZONING_STAGING_REGISTRY entry for Elgin's Travis-side FeatureServer/1 (mirroring legacy-design-tools' own elgin-tx-travis entry in zoning-layers.ts: same layerUrl, same codeDomainMap, layerWhere CITY_LIMIT='ELGIN', county 48453, presumably cityKey 'elgin-tx' to match layer 0's row so parcel-r5-zoning's per-city logic treats them as one city, though this needs confirming against how parcel-r5-zoning keys city_key vs county for its residue accounting), then run stage-tx-zoning-district.mjs with ZONING_STAGING_PATH=1 --apply against CORTEX_DATABASE_URL. Requires a hauska-engine worktree and explicit write authorization, neither of which this dispatch granted.

Bastrop (48021) and Travis (48453) remain held on parcel-r5-zoning's LAYER_GAP_RESIDUE_EXCEEDED refusal. This close does not move that number. Two counties are still waiting; recommend the operator either re-dispatch to a hauska-engine-scoped lane or explicitly authorize this lane to open one.

Once layer 1 is genuinely staged (whichever lane does it), re-measuring the residue per this dispatch's steps 3-4 and comparing to CTX-ELGIN's probed 9 (48021) / 457 (48453) is still the correct next step -- that part of the dispatch's design was sound; only the file pointer for step 2 was wrong.
